source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἰδιωτικοὺς ψαλμοὺς λέγεσθαι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, οὐδὲ ἀκανόνιστα βιβλία, ἀλλὰ μόνα τὰ κανονικὰ τῆς καινῆς καὶ παλαιᾶς διαθήκης.
orientation: The council is giving a rule about what may be read or sung in church, just before it lists the canonical books.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary for private psalms to be said in the church, nor uncanonical books, but only the canonical ones of the new and old covenant.

choices.why: The adjective means privately composed or belonging to an individual, as opposed to the canonical Psalter; 'private' preserves the contrast with the church's authorized texts.
The verb covers recitation and singing of texts in worship; 'said' is the literal rendering and keeps the liturgical context open.
The term is the negative of 'canonical' and refers to books outside the authorized list; 'uncanonical' matches the glossary's 'canonical books' terminology.

choices.english: of the new and old covenant
choices.why: The phrase names the two parts of the canon; 'covenant' is the literal sense of διαθήκη, and the word order 'new and old' follows the source.
rejected: of the New and Old Testament
of the new and old testament

pass_b_english: Private psalms must not be said in church, nor uncanonical books, but only the canonical books of the new and old covenant.
